coordinate_convention: zero-based pixel indices; x right, y down (screen); (x,y) = column x, row y; boxes [left, top, right, bottom] exclusive right/bottom; angles from +x, positive = descending to the right on screen

The same convention is used in render-review.json line 41. Angles below are measured from the horizontal; 'descends right' means +x,+y on screen and 'ascends right' means +x,-y.

quoted_endpoint_identity.(4,8): opaque single-pixel cap of the left arm (row 8 run [4,4]); directly above the centre of the row-9 3-pixel run [3,5]. It is the top tip of the short arm, not a point on a 45-degree stroke contour.
quoted_endpoint_identity.(6,12): opaque single-pixel bottom tip (row 12 run [6,6]); directly below the centre of the row-11 run [5,7]. The two strokes merge in rows 10 (run [4,8]) and 11 (run [5,7]); (6,12) is the lowest tip pixel of that merge.
quoted_endpoint_identity.(12,4): opaque single-pixel cap of the right arm (row 4 run [12,12]); directly above the centre of the row-5 run [11,13].

verdicts.about_1_to_2_as_approximate_visual_propo: acceptable only when labelled approximate; the exact 1:2 belongs to the vertical row extents (4 rows vs 8 rows), and the measured axis ratio is 2.24

what_the_old_numbers_measured.row_extent_ratio: 4 : 8 = 1 : 2 (exact, but these are vertical row spans, not 45-degree axis lengths)
what_the_old_numbers_measured.if_axes_were_45_degrees: a 45-degree segment spanning 4 rows would also span 4 columns (length 4*sqrt(2) = 5.657) and one spanning 8 rows would span 8 columns (length 11.314); the quoted endpoints span 2 and 6 columns instead

column_partition.rule: x <= 5 | x == 6 | x >= 7 (column ranges only; not a geometric arm model)

contours.reading: Between the single-pixel caps and the merge, the stroke contours advance exactly one column per row in one direction (monotonic), i.e. the 3-pixel-run staircases are built on 45-degree diagonals. At each cap the outer edge reverses direction by one column (left edge 4 -> 3 -> 4 ..., right edge 12 -> 13 -> 12 ...) because the cap sits directly above the centre of the adjacent 3-pixel run; a straight line through a cap and the vertex pixel is therefore NOT a 45-degree line.

A_run_centres_excluding_caps.definition: straight line through the centres of 3-pixel runs only: left arm row 9 run [3,5] centre (4,9) to row 11 run [5,7] centre (6,11); right arm row 5 run [11,13] centre (12,5) to the same row 11 centre (6,11). Excludes the single-pixel caps (4,8), (12,4) and (6,12) and the merged 5-pixel row 10.

B_outer_contours.definition: outer contour staircases: left arm's left edge from (3,9) to the vertex pixel (6,12); right arm's right edge from (13,5) to (6,12). Caps excluded.

C_principal_axis_per_partition.definition: least-squares principal axis through the pixel centres of each column partition (x<=5 and x>=7); the shared column 6 excluded. This is a statistical fit, not the quoted tip-to-tip line.

claims.finding: The segment (6,12)->(12,4) has delta [6, -8], length 10.0 and lies 53.13 degrees above the horizontal (ascending right). Not a 45-degree line; 8 is the vertical row extent rows 4..12 (12-4), the column extent is 6.

claims.status: corrected (explanation); approximate visual proportion retained as approximate
claims.finding: Along the quoted tip-to-tip lines the length ratio is 10/sqrt(20) = sqrt(5) = 2.236, not 2. The 4:8 = 1:2 ratio is exact only as a ratio of vertical row extents. Other defensible centreline estimates give 3.0 (3-pixel run centres excluding caps), 2.33 (outer contours) and 2.76 (principal-axis extents). 'About 1:2' remains acceptable only as approximate visual-proportion language (long arm roughly twice the short arm by eye and by row span); it is not a measured ratio of 45-degree axis lengths.

claims.quoted: "Both arms are exact 45-degree diagonals, so each contour steps one pixel per row with uniform run lengths"
claims.status: corrected in part; stroke-construction part supported
claims.finding: The stroke contours between the caps and the merge DO step exactly one column per row in one direction (left-arm left edge rows 9..12 = 3,4,5,6; right-arm right edge rows 5..12 = 13..6; right-arm left edge rows 4..9 = 12..7), so the 3-pixel-run staircases are built on 45-degree diagonals and the edge-rhythm check holds for the strokes. But the arm AXES through the quoted endpoints are 63.4 and 53.1 degrees, because each single-pixel cap sits directly above the centre of its adjacent 3-pixel run (edge reverses by one column at the cap). 'Exact 45-degree diagonals' is true of the stroke staircases, false of the tip-to-tip axes.
Repeats the row-extent figures under the name 'axis steps'. 4 and 8 are row extents rows 8..12 and 4..12; axis lengths through the quoted endpoints are sqrt(20) and 10 (ratio sqrt(5)).
